13 % 4

What will be the output of the following Python expression? print(2 ** 3 ** 2)
print(2 ** 3 ** 2)
  • a) 64
  • b) 512
  • c) 256
  • d) 81
column2:
Correct Answer: B
The exponentiation operator (**) has right-to-left associativity. Therefore, 2 ** 3 ** 2 is evaluated as 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512.

  • a) Addition, Multiplication, Exponentiation
  • b) Exponentiation, Multiplication, Addition
  • c) Multiplication, Exponentiation, Addition

What will be the output of the following Python code?
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)
  • a) [1, 2, 3]
  • b) [1, 2, 3, 4]
  • c) [4, 1, 2, 3]
  • d) AttributeError
column2:
Correct Answer: B
Lists in Python are mutable objects. Assigning b = a creates a reference to the same list object in memory, so mutating b also affects a.
